did_you_know.text: Bashan lies east of the Jordan and is a volcanic region rich in dark basalt stones. Its volcanic soil can be very fertile.
Mount Hermon was known by different names among the peoples who lived around it. This shows that it was an important landmark throughout the region.

A cubit was an ancient unit of length, roughly the distance from the elbow to the fingertips, though its size was not exactly fixed. So the measurements of Og’s bed are approximate rather than precise modern measurements.
In the Bible, the term “Rephaim” is not used only for an ancient people; elsewhere it is also associated with the dead in the underworld. Its meaning depends on the context.
In place-names, the word “havvot” does not necessarily mean a farm; it can refer to a settlement or group of settlements. Thus “Havvoth-jair” means Jair’s settlements.
The Jordan flows from the Sea of Galilee to the Dead Sea, a salty lake with no outlet to the ocean. Water evaporates from it, causing salts to build up.
The Hebrew word “chalutzim” is connected with the idea of being equipped and ready. In a military context, it describes the force marching at the front of the camp.
These verses emphasize that mutual responsibility does not end when one tribe receives its territory. Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh must help the others until they too receive their inheritance.
The name “Lebanon” is probably related to the Hebrew word for “white,” perhaps because of the mountains’ snow-covered peaks or pale rocks. The exact origin of the name is not completely certain.
The expression “rav lakh” literally means “it is enough for you” or “enough.” Here it is a brief and decisive reply to Moses’ request.
